experiments.hypothesis_name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts

model_fitness.best_available_model: SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons in compartmentalized (microfluidic) culture; no validated in vivo SPG8 model exists (EVIDENCE, MONDO:0011339 - pathology inferred from HSP as a class)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially: iPSC neurons carry the patient WASHC5 allele and could show endosomal/transport phenotypes, but the proposed modality acts on an intracellular cytoskeletal/transport compartment for which no extracellular receptor interface has been identified (INFERENCE, supportive of the delivery objection)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes for cortical projection neuron identity in vitro; no model reproduces the full-length human corticospinal axon where the therapeutic compartment lies (INFERENCE)
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Cargo transport velocity/flux, distal neurite degeneration index, tubulin acetylation - all measurable; but none of these would be engaged by a systemically or intrathecally dosed biologic in vivo (INFERENCE)
model_fitness.important_limitations: No in vivo SPG8 system; trophic-biologic effects in dish are not predictive of CNS exposure in patients; prior neurotrophic biologics (BDNF, CNTF, GDNF, IGF-1) failed in motor neuron disease substantially on CNS exposure grounds (INFERENCE, contradictory)

plan.critical_question: Before any protein-modality program, the only question worth money is a prerequisite one: does any extracellular or cell-surface mediator sit between WASH-complex failure and distal axonal dieback in SPG8 neurons - i.e. is there anything at all for a biologic to bind? Absent that, the modality is excluded by target-compartment mismatch, not by potency or PK (INFERENCE).
plan.proposed_experiment: Do not run a therapeutic experiment with this modality. Run a single cheap target-discovery screen instead: surface proteomics (cell-surface biotinylation plus mass spectrometry) and secretome profiling of SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons versus isogenic-corrected controls, to ask whether the WASHC5 variant produces any reproducible change in surface receptor repertoire or secreted mediators. Pair with a conditioned-medium transfer test (does SPG8-neuron medium impair neurite maintenance in control neurons, and vice versa). Total scope: one cell line pair, two assays, no animals, no biologic manufactured.
plan.model: SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons with isogenic CRISPR-corrected control (model cells named in the disease brief); fibroblasts as an inexpensive pre-screen
plan.primary_readout: Differential surface/secreted protein abundance (SPG8 vs isogenic control) and neurite-maintenance effect of conditioned-medium transfer
plan.supportive_result: A reproducible, mechanism-linked surface receptor or secreted mediator is altered in SPG8 neurons (e.g. a mis-sorted receptor retained or depleted at the surface as a consequence of WASH-dependent recycling failure), and/or conditioned medium transfers a maintenance deficit. This would create an actual extracellular interface and would justify reopening the protein modality.
plan.negative_result: No reproducible surface or secreted difference and no transferable conditioned-medium effect. The perturbation remains entirely intracellular, confirming that enzyme/protein replacement is mechanistically excluded (strumpellin is an obligate cytosolic multiprotein-complex subunit, INFERENCE) and that trophic/anti-inhibitor biologics would be non-specific neuroprotection with no SPG8 rationale.
plan.decision_enabled: Negative (the likely outcome): close the protein modality for SPG8 permanently and redirect the budget to the small-molecule transport experiment and to resolving dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency. Supportive: define the newly identified surface node as a separate target and re-enter the normal biologics triage, including the unresolved CNS-delivery question. Either way the decision costs one iPSC experiment rather than a biologic program.

experiments.hypothesis_name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts

model_fitness.best_available_model: SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons with isogenic CRISPR-corrected control, grown in microfluidic/compartmentalized culture that physically separates soma from distal axon; HDAC6-inhibitor transport-rescue assays are established in inherited axonopathy neurons (EVIDENCE, PMID:31845794) and in vivo in CMT2D mice (EVIDENCE, PMID:29520015)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially. The culture carries the causal human allele and permits direct measurement of the two things the hypothesis asserts - bidirectional cargo transport and tubulin acetylation. It does not capture corticospinal tract length, decades of ageing, or spasticity. Critically, the mechanistic bridge from actin-based WASH sorting failure to microtubule-based transport failure is assumed, not shown (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:30061306).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes - iPSC-derived cortical/layer-V-like projection neurons are the disease-relevant cell class; the distal-axon compartment is approximated, not reproduced, by microfluidic chambers (INFERENCE)
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Alpha-tubulin acetylation (western/immunofluorescence), live-imaging kinetics of mitochondrial and endolysosomal cargo transport (velocity, run length, anterograde:retrograde flux, pause frequency), and distal neurite fragmentation/degeneration index over time
model_fitness.important_limitations: No validated in vivo SPG8 model exists (EVIDENCE, MONDO:0011339), so a positive cellular result cannot be converted into a motor-benefit demonstration without building one; HDAC6 inhibition improves transport in many neurons regardless of baseline deficit, creating a high false-positive risk; iPSC neurons are developmentally immature relative to adult corticospinal neurons

plan.critical_question: Do SPG8 patient neurons actually have a measurable axonal cargo-transport and/or tubulin-acetylation deficit relative to isogenic controls? Everything downstream depends on this, and it has not been shown for WASHC5 in anything we retrieved (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
plan.proposed_experiment: Two-stage, single-protocol experiment. Stage 1 (phenotype, must precede any drug): culture SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons and isogenic CRISPR-corrected controls (>=2 independent patient lines carrying distinct missense variants, >=3 differentiations each) in microfluidic devices; quantify baseline alpha-tubulin acetylation in the distal axon compartment and live-image bidirectional transport of mitochondria and of a labelled endolysosomal cargo; score distal neurite degeneration at a late timepoint. Pre-register effect-size and significance thresholds before unblinding genotype. Stage 2 (pharmacology, run ONLY if Stage 1 is positive): dose-response with a selective CNS-penetrant HDAC6 inhibitor (EKZ-438-class, 12 nM potency, >8500-fold selective, EVIDENCE PMID:41061670; tubastatin A as tool comparator, EVIDENCE PMID:29520015), with the acetylation increase measured in parallel as the pharmacodynamic control. Decisive design feature: the isogenic control must be dosed alongside, and the rescue must be genotype-selective - a larger effect in SPG8 than in control neurons at the same acetylation increase. A drug effect of equal magnitude in both genotypes is a null result for this hypothesis, not a hit.
plan.model: SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons plus isogenic corrected controls in compartmentalized microfluidic culture (patient fibroblasts/iPSC neurons are the named accessible model cells for this disease)
plan.primary_readout: Stage 1: genotype difference in distal-axon cargo transport flux and alpha-tubulin acetylation. Stage 2: genotype-selective normalization of transport and of distal neurite degeneration by HDAC6 inhibition, at a pharmacodynamically confirmed acetylation increase.
plan.supportive_result: SPG8 neurons show a reproducible transport deficit and/or reduced tubulin acetylation across independent lines, and HDAC6 inhibition restores transport toward isogenic-control levels with a significantly larger effect in SPG8 than in control neurons, and reduces distal degeneration.
plan.negative_result: No baseline transport or acetylation difference between SPG8 and isogenic neurons (kills the hypothesis at Stage 1, before any drug is bought); or a transport deficit exists but HDAC6 inhibition improves transport equally in patient and control neurons - a generic pharmacodynamic effect with no SPG8-specific benefit, which is the pre-specified failure mode of this approach.
plan.decision_enabled: Stage 1 negative: drop the axonal-transport hypothesis for SPG8 entirely and redirect to resolving dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency and to endolysosomal/cargo-mis-sorting phenotypes, which remain the better-supported biology (EVIDENCE, PMID:30061306). Stage 1 positive but Stage 2 non-selective: deprioritize HDAC6 - do not advance on a disease-irrelevant pharmacodynamic effect - but keep the transport deficit as a validated biomarker for other agents. Both positive: commit to building the missing in vivo system (a knock-in mouse carrying a patient missense variant, which the disease brief lists as a major unknown) before any clinical consideration; a cellular rescue alone is not sufficient to enter an ultra-rare, rapidly progressing population with no animal model and no biomarker.
